description:
Younger Americans feel that they don’t have a say in their country’s policies and future, argues Samuel Moyn, who teaches history and law at Yale University.
 
Moyn tells host Steve Clemons that the generational divide between old and young is widening, in the US and around the world. In the US, where protest is shunned and young politicians are not the norm, many people feel “my vote wouldn’t make a difference,” says Moyn.
 
With increasing lifespans comes an aging population, and power is “hoarded” by older, wealthier citizens – leading to gerontocracy (rule by elders) instead of democracy, Moyn explains.

description: US President Donald Trump says Russia and Ukraine have agreed to an immediate ceasefire covering attacks on each other's energy infrastructure, although neither Kyiv nor Moscow has confirmed the agreement. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had earlier proposed an energy ceasefire while criticising Washington's decision to ease sanctions on Russian diesel exports. Trump has blamed Ukraine for rising diesel prices and suggested Zelenskyy should be replaced, prompting the Ukrainian president to offer to hold elections if Russia agrees to a 60-day ceasefire. The US decision to allow Russian diesel onto global markets has also drawn criticism from Democrats and Republicans, who warn that the revenue could help fund Moscow's war. In Kyiv, a senior Ukrainian official says no agreement has been communicated, while Ukrainians question whether halting strikes on Russian oil facilities

Israeli fighter jets struck a residential neighbourhood in Deir el-Balah in central Gaza late on Saturday, destroying homes and leaving families displaced. 
Residents say a building that housed more than 300 people was destroyed, forcing women and children to sleep in the open after losing their homes and belongings. 
The attack has added to Gaza's worsening housing crisis, with thousands of families already displaced and struggling to find shelter. 
Bulldozers are clearing debris from the streets as residents search through the rubble for their possessions. 
Israeli attacks have also been reported elsewhere in the Gaza Strip, raising further concerns about civilian safety. 
A year after the ceasefire was presented as a pathway towards reconstruction and a return to normal life, Palestinians continue to face destruction, displacement and uncertainty.

The United States is stepping up its campaign against the International Criminal Court, with new sanctions threatening to disrupt its operations.

The ICC prosecutes individuals accused of genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity. The Trump administration accuses it of targeting American and Israeli officials. 

The sanctions follow earlier US measures against the court’s president, judges and senior prosecutors. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio says the latest move will restrict transactions with the ICC.

Several European countries, alongside Canada and Japan, have reaffirmed their support for the court. A joint statement said the sanctions, if implemented, “will have a significant impact on the Court’s work, its dedicated staff and their families”. 

The dispute fell on the same day former ICC judge and UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Navi Pillay was announced as this year’s Nobel Peace Prize laureate.

Al Jazeera’s Lou Browne reports.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Maximilian Hess, a fellow at the Foreign Policy Research Institute and founder of the political risk consultancy Enmetena Advisory, speaking from London, says Donald Trump’s diesel deal with Vladimir Putin won't meaningfully affect US oil markets.

Hess says the initial 300,000 tons of Russian diesel is less than a day of US transport diesel use, and further amounts would be only a few days’ worth. He says it is unclear whether Russia can deliver, as it has not exported diesel since July because of Ukrainian strikes.

He calls the move “far more rhetorical” than a new sanctions move, noting that one-month waivers covered almost all Russian crude in March and April. He says the Lindsey Graham sanctions act has an October 19 deadline for some new measures. It puts sanctions in law, making them harder for Trump to lift, though he can suspend many. The suspension is written for six months.

Israel says it is targeting threats from Hamas, while Hamas says Israel is breaking the agreement. Israeli forces control roughly two-thirds of the territory, and tens of thousands of families remain in makeshift shelters.

Mark Lattimer, executive director of the Ceasefire Centre for Civilian Rights and an author on civilian protection during conflict, speaking from London, says there has not really been a ceasefire, with the Israeli military continuing regular attacks. 

He says Phase 1 was relatively successful, with the remaining 20 living Israeli hostages released and about 2,000 Palestinian prisoners freed, but that the killing has gone on since.
